newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depo rates. forwards soar as ecu/drs firms.
newsitem.headline: Greek depo rates. forwards soar as ecu/drs firms.

text.p: Greek money market and forex forwards were surging and fixed coupon bonds were losing ground on the back of forex outflows and a weaker drachma vis-a-vis the ecu and the mark, traders said.
"Depo rates and implied drachma rates from forex forwards have jumped," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "The market is nervous fearing that forex outflows will continue at the fixing today."
Implied drachma rates in some tenors have even risen above depo rates, dealers said.
"There is pressure and interest rates have been rising since this morning," said a dealer at a private bank. "They have jumped a point or more in some tenors."
Forex dealers said ecu/drachma remained well bid piercing the 312.50 hurdle and they expected renewed forex outflows at today's fixing.

The central bank sold 200 million ecus and 25 million marks to support the drachma at the fixing on Thursday. It intervened again on Wednesday to prop up the local currency selling 350 million ecus and 80 million marks.

"Mark/drachma has gained ground on a softer ecu/mark," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The drachma has been drifting lower against the ecu trading above 312.50 and the central bank has checked $/drachma rates twice so far."
Bank of Greece checks $/drachma rates to send a signal that it will intervene.

"I have no doubt that the central bank will sell large amounts of $, marks and ecus at the fixing to back up the drachma," the dealer said. "I expect ecu/drachma to trade lower than current levels after the fixing."
Bonds were also under pressure with prices of three- and seven-year fixed coupon bonds shedding 40 to 60 basis points, bond dealers said.
"The sentiment has changed and bonds are under pressure," said a bond dealer at a foreign bank. "I see less pressure on FRNs and even some switching out of FRNs into five-year bonds."
Dealers said the rising cost of interbank funding was the major factor behind the selling pressure on bonds.
"It is ecu/drachma and forex outflows that have squeezed interbank liquidity and led to much higher interest rates which in turn have hit bonds," a dealer said.
The finance ministry said it would auction 100 billion drachmas of 10-year, fixed coupon bonds and re-open bids for 50 billion drachmas each of three-, five- and seven-year bonds on June 17.
The treasury will issue 12-month T-bills at 9.60 percent on June 2, down 10 basis points, reopen bids for three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds and auction 10-year fixed coupon bonds on June 19.
Greece auctioned three-year, 9.80 percent bonds, five-year, 9.20 percent bonds and seven-year, 8.9 percent bonds on March 19.
The mark was quoted at 160.62/67 from Wednesday's 160.135 fix, the dollar at 273.37/47 drachmas from 272.22 and the ecu at 312.53/63 from 311.950 drachmas.

** Overnight at 9.90-10.40
** One week at 11.40-11.90
** Two weeks at 11.40-11.90
** Three weeks at 11.40-11.90
** One month at 11.40-11.90
** Two months at 11.40-11.90
** Three months at 11.20-11.70
** Six months at 10.40-10.90
** Nine months at 10.00-10.50
